advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the literal `"render"` in `renderable_units` with `wiki_render._RENDER` to match the consuming test's alignment.
advisory.finding: generate_dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.py filters segmenter units with the string literal "render" instead of the shared wiki_render._RENDER constant that the consuming hardening test uses; if _RENDER's value ever changes, the generator would silently select the wrong units while the test keeps aligning, breaking the byte-equivalence contract without an obvious failure at the generator.
scenarios: A future rename/retag of the _RENDER kind constant in wiki_render leaves the generator selecting stale units while the hardening test tracks the new constant.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use `if kind == wiki_render._RENDER` in renderable_units, mirroring the hardening test.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reap the Pandoc process group on timeout in legacy_convert (or document that regeneration may orphan a grandchild), matching production _convert's d843 hardening.
evidence: scripts/generate_dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.py:170-184: `completed = runner([...], input=markdown, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30, check=False)`
wiki_render.py:9-11: "``subprocess.run(timeout=...)`` reaps only the DIRECT child. A pipe-holding grandchild survives it and keeps burning CPU (bug d843, bpo-30154)"
advisory.finding: legacy_convert runs Pandoc via subprocess.run(timeout=30) without start_new_session/process-group reaping; per the wiki_render module's own d843 documentation, subprocess.run(timeout=...) reaps only the direct child, so a pipe-holding grandchild spawned by a pathological corpus unit survives and keeps burning CPU during fixture regeneration — the exact hazard production _convert was hardened against.
scenarios: Regenerating the fixture over a pathological corpus body that spins Pandoc; the 30s timeout fires but a grandchild survives and spins at full CPU.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure a CI lane installs the `wiki` extra and runs `test_wiki_render_hardening.py` so the byte-equivalence and stdin-contract assertions actually gate (or document why they are intentionally non-gating).
evidence: tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_hardening.py:60: `_NEEDS_PANDOC = pytest.mark.skipif(_PANDOC is None, reason="the `wiki` extra is not installed")`

`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:323`: `uv sync --locked --extra dev --extra reviewbot --extra ui ...` — the default pytest lane does not install `wiki`, so `_pandoc_path()` is None and the byte-equivalence + stdin tests skip

`.github/workflows/_optionality.yml:184` lists `wiki:wiki` but that lane (lines 188-...) only installs+probes each extra; the only pytest invocation in the file (lines 119-122) targets `tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_optionality.py` and one completion-gate test, not this suite
ABSENCE: `search_files` for `--extra wiki` and for any pytest run over `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` with pandoc present returned no matches across `.github/workflows`
advisory.finding: The load-bearing behavior-preservation assertion — byte-identical rendered output vs the landed renderer — is guarded by `_NEEDS_PANDOC` (skipif `_pandoc_path() is None`), and no determinable CI lane installs the `wiki` extra while running this suite, so it never gates. The default pytest lane installs only `dev + reviewbot + ui`; the `wiki` optionality lane only install/import-probes and runs pytest against two unrelated degradation test files.
scenarios: A future edit to `_convert` that alters WHAT pandoc produces (e.g. dropping the anchor-strip or trailing-newline rstrip) would pass every gating CI lane because the only test comparing bytes is skipped for lack of the `wiki` extra.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a CI lane (or extend an existing one) that runs `uv sync --extra wiki` and executes `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_hardening.py`, so `_NEEDS_PANDOC`-guarded byte-equivalence tests run at least once per Verified gate.
